_schema.purpose: Scene geometry of the Sekisovskoye twin (spec 4.2). Generated by sekis/geometry.py from params.json, registry.json and model/terrain/; regenerate with `python -m sekis.geometry` in team/.
_schema.frame: x east, y up = elevation in metres above sea level, z south; 1 unit = 1 m on every axis. x and z are UTM 44N easting and southing from the mine point (frame.origin). Points are [x, y, z]; plan pairs are [x, z].
_schema.numbers: Coordinates and lengths are rounded to 0.1 m. section_m2, slope_deg, bearing_deg, length_factor, spacing, density_t_m3 and the *_deg slopes keep their own precision.
_schema.terrain: The ground. rows[j][i] is the elevation at x = origin[0] + i * spacing, z = origin[1] + j * spacing (row 0 north, column 0 west); each cell is two triangles split along its south-west to north-east diagonal (three.js PlaneGeometry vertex order). inset is a finer grid over the old pit that replaces the main-grid cells cells[0]..cells[2]-1 (x) by cells[1]..cells[3]-1 (z) without cracks. texture is a north-up image whose edges are extent. Show attribution with the scene.
_schema.profile: Ground elevation along the long section: points [x, y] every step metres of x at z.
_schema.objects: One entry per registry thing that has a place in the scene, keyed by thing ID, in registry order. Every entry has kind, primitive, sourced, planned and anchor (label and click point), then source (what the position and size rest on).
_schema.scenery: Drawable items that are not things: surface, old pit, haul roads, yard, water courses, village, industrial zone, unnumbered tailings cells, pipelines, backfilled blocks. Keyed by a local name; each has primitive, sourced and source.
_schema.sourced: Underground: true when the elevations, cross-section or bearing drawn are published figures; plan positions underground are schematic for every object (plan: schematic). Surface: true when the position is read from OpenStreetMap or the Sentinel-2 image (sizes may still come from the documents); false when the place was chosen because the object is not identifiable.
_schema.planned: true: the thing is in state planned in the registry (draw dashed). On a link or a decline node it marks a connection below the workings developed at the start. planned_below on an airway is the elevation under which the airway is design only.

primitives.pit: the old open pit: outline [[x,z]] (OSM rim polygon), rim [[x,y,z]] (where the carved wall meets the DEM), floor (elevation) with floor_outline [[x,z]], base [x,floor,z] (floor centre), top (highest rim point), benches [{y, lines [[[x,z],...]]}] (crest lines at each bench elevation), section [[x,y]] (lowest ground per 10 m of x: the pit projected on the long section). The carved ground itself is in terrain.
primitives.cone: base [x,y,z], radius and height at reference_t tonnes
primitives.prism: footprint [[x,z],...] extruded from bottom to top (elevations)
primitives.polyline: points [[x,y,z],...]; width and height of the opening where it is a drive
primitives.marker: a point; the position is anchor

_schema.decline: points run from the portal to the design bottom, every segment at slope_deg. bottom_elevation is the face at the start (the live value is the twin feature of the same name). nodes are the passing bays: the portal and every 25 m of elevation below it; chainage is metres along points from the portal; type is portal, bay, turn or access (a turn with a level access). Haul distance for travel times is chainage x length_factor.
_schema.level: points is the level drive. links leave the drive: role access (to a decline), crosscut (to a stope), airway (to a shaft or raise), chamber (to a pump station). extent is [x_min, z_min, x_max, z_max] of the level's workings.
_schema.stope: a vertical tabular block: size [strike_length, height, thickness] with height the 50 m floor, thickness stope.thickness_m and strike_length = tonnage_t / (density_t_m3 x height x thickness).
_schema.mobile: trucks, loaders and rigs carry mobile true; their box stands on its parking slot. Live positions are the twin features pos_x, pos_y, pos_z.
_schema.surface: Surface objects stand on the terrain: a box or prism bottom is the lowest ground under its footprint; markers, cones and line vertices are at the ground; a settling pond's water surface is the ground at its centre. A tailings prism's top is the level that holds the dam's capacity_m3 between the ground and the top. Shaft collars are at the ground of their position (the registry collar elevation is kept as documented_top).

frame.origin: x = 0, z = 0 is the mine point 50.3286583 N, 82.5966139 E (50 deg 19'43.17" N, 82 deg 35'47.81" E); y = 0 is sea level
frame.crs: x = UTM 44N easting - 613640.00, z = 5576392.36 - UTM 44N northing (EPSG:32644, WGS 84); grid north is the scene's north
frame.layout: underground plan positions are schematic: the mine layout (ore zone, declines, airways, levels) is shifted by layout_shift so that the TU2 portal stands on the centre of the carved pit floor; surface positions are real (sourced flags)

terrain.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (TanDEM-X 2011-2015), cell means over 62.5 m; inside the OSM pit outline the final pit carved to the documents (floor +320 m, benched wall at its overall slope); built offline by tools/build_terrain.py
